title.en: Volume 85 Biographies 50: Yuwen Huaji, Yuwen Zhiji, Wang Shichong
title.raw: 卷85 列傳第50 序言 宇文化及 司馬德戡 裴虔通 王充 段達 Volume 85 Biographies 50: Yuwen Huaji, Yuwen Zhiji, Wang Shichong

sentences.zh: 序夫肖形天地，人稱最靈，以其知父子之道，識君臣之義，異夫禽獸者也。

translations.literal: Preface: Taking their form from heaven and earth, humans are called the most spiritual, because they know the way of father and son and understand the righteousness of ruler and minister, differing from birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: Preface: Shaped in the image of heaven and earth, humankind is deemed the most sentient of creatures, for people grasp the bonds between father and son and the duties between ruler and subject—qualities that set them apart from beasts.

sentences.zh: 傳曰：「人生在三，事之如一。」

translations.literal: The Classic says: "A person is born under three [obligations], and serving them is one and the same."
translations.idiomatic: The tradition says: "From birth a person stands under three obligations, and to serve them all is one and the same duty."

sentences.zh: 然則君臣父子，其道不殊，父不可以不父，子不可以不子，君不可以不君，臣不可以不臣。

translations.literal: Thus ruler and minister, father and son—their Way is not different: a father cannot fail to be a father, a son cannot fail to be a son, a ruler cannot fail to be a ruler, a minister cannot fail to be a minister.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the principles governing ruler and subject, father and son, are fundamentally the same: a father must be a father, a son must be a son, a sovereign must be a sovereign, and a minister must be a minister.

sentences.zh: 故曰君猶天也，天可讎乎！

translations.literal: Therefore it is said that the ruler is like heaven—can one take revenge upon heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying that the ruler is like heaven itself—who could dream of turning against heaven?

sentences.zh: 是以有罪歸刑，見危授命，竭忠貞以立節，不臨難而苟免。

translations.literal: Therefore when guilty one accepts punishment; when facing danger one gives one's life; one exhausts loyalty and integrity to establish one's principles and does not seek easy escape when hardship comes.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason the loyal accept punishment when they err, surrender their lives when danger threatens, exhaust fidelity and integrity to uphold their honor, and never seek an easy escape in the face of peril.

sentences.zh: 故聞其風者，懷夫慷慨，千載之後，莫不願以為臣。

translations.literal: Therefore those who hear of such conduct are filled with ardent admiration; even a thousand years later, none fail to wish to serve as their ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Those who hear of such virtue are stirred to noble feeling, and even a millennium later none who learn of them fail to wish they might have served such masters.

sentences.zh: 此其所以生榮死哀，取貴前哲者矣。

translations.literal: This is why they are honored in life and mourned in death, and why they are esteemed by the wise of former ages.
translations.idiomatic: This is what wins them glory in life and lamentation in death, and what earns them the esteem of sages past.

sentences.zh: 至於委質策名，代卿世祿，出受心膂之寄，入參帷幄之謀，身處機衡，肆趙高之姦宄，世荷權寵，行王莽之桀逆，生靈之所讎疾，犬豕不食其餘。

translations.literal: As for those who pledge their bodies and register their names, who inherit ministerial rank and hereditary stipends, who go forth entrusted as the ruler's backbone and enter to take part in counsel within the curtains, who occupy the pivot of power and give free rein to treachery like Zhao Gao's, who generation after generation bear favor and power and act with Wang Mang's violent rebellion—the living hate them as enemies, and even dogs and pigs will not eat what remains of them.
translations.idiomatic: But those who pledge allegiance and register their names, who inherit noble rank and hereditary stipends, who abroad receive the ruler's deepest trust and at court join deliberations in the inner council, who hold the levers of power and unleash treachery like Zhao Gao's, who enjoy privilege generation after generation and commit outrage like Wang Mang's—the living loathe them as enemies, and even dogs and swine will not touch their remains.

sentences.zh: 雖薦社污宮，彰必誅之釁，斵棺焚骨，明篡殺之咎，可以懲夫既往，未足深誡將來。

translations.literal: Although offering them to the earth god and defiling their ancestral shrines makes clear the crime that must be punished, and smashing their coffins and burning their bones makes plain the guilt of usurpation and murder, this can chastise the past but is not sufficient to warn the future deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Though dragging their bodies to the altars of earth and defiling their ancestral halls exposes crimes deserving death, and smashing their coffins and burning their bones makes clear the guilt of usurpation and murder, such punishments may chastise the dead but are not enough to warn those yet to come.

sentences.zh: 昔孔子修春秋，而亂臣賊子知懼，抑使之求名不得，欲蓋而彰者也。

translations.literal: Formerly when Confucius compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals, rebellious ministers and wicked sons knew fear; he restrained them so that they could not obtain the fame they sought—wishing to conceal their deeds, they only made them more conspicuous.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, when Confucius compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals, rebellious ministers and traitorous sons learned to fear, for he denied them the fame they craved—those who sought to hide their deeds only made them more conspicuous.

sentences.zh: 今故正其罪名，以冠於篇首，庶後之君子見作者之意焉。

translations.literal: Now we therefore set right their crimes and place their names at the head of the chapter, so that later gentlemen may see the author's intent.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore set forth their crimes by name at the head of this chapter, so that later readers may grasp the historian's intent.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及，左翊衞大將軍述之子也。

translations.literal: Yuwen Huaji—Yuwen Huaji was the son of Yuwen Shu, General-in-Chief of the Left Yiwu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Huaji was the son of Yuwen Shu, General-in-Chief of the Left Yiwu Guard.

sentences.zh: 性兇險，不循法度，好乘肥挾彈，馳騖道中，由是長安謂之輕薄公子。

translations.literal: His nature was fierce and dangerous; he did not follow the law. He loved to ride fat horses and carry slingshots, galloping recklessly along the roads, for which reason Chang'an called him a frivolous young lord.
translations.idiomatic: Violent and unscrupulous by nature, he scorned the law, loved to ride blooded mounts with a sling at his side, and careered recklessly through the streets, so that Chang'an dubbed him a dissolute young rake.

sentences.zh: 煬帝為太子時，常領千牛，出入臥內。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang was crown prince, Huaji often led the Thousand-Ox guard and went in and out of the sleeping quarters.
translations.idiomatic: While Yang Guang was still crown prince, Huaji often commanded the Thousand-Ox guard and came and went freely within the heir's private apartments.

sentences.zh: 累遷至太子僕。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted until he reached the post of Master of the Heir's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to Master of the Heir's Household.

sentences.zh: 數以受納貨賄，再三免官。

translations.literal: Several times he was found accepting bribes and was repeatedly dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly caught taking bribes and dismissed from office again and again.

sentences.zh: 太子嬖昵之，俄而復職。

translations.literal: The crown prince favored and was intimate with him, and before long he was restored to his post.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince doted on him, and he was soon restored to office each time.

sentences.zh: 又以其弟士及尚南陽公主。

translations.literal: Moreover, because his younger brother Shiji married Princess Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: His standing rose further when his younger brother Shiji married Princess Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 化及由此益驕，處公卿間，言辭不遜，多所陵轢。

translations.literal: Because of this Huaji grew ever more arrogant; among the high ministers his speech was disrespectful and he often bullied others.
translations.idiomatic: Emboldened by this connection, Huaji grew ever more arrogant among the high officials, speaking with insolence and bullying many.

sentences.zh: 見人子女狗馬珍玩，必請託求之。

translations.literal: Whenever he saw someone's children, dogs, horses, or precious curios, he was sure to ask and demand them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he saw another man's children, horses, dogs, or precious curios, he would demand them as gifts.

sentences.zh: 常與屠販者遊，以規其利。

translations.literal: He often associated with butchers and peddlers to scheme for profit.
translations.idiomatic: He often consorted with butchers and peddlers to squeeze profit from them.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，拜太僕少卿，益恃舊恩，貪冒尤甚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Huaji was appointed Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud; he relied all the more on old favor and his greed and corruption grew especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Guang ascended the throne, Huaji was made Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud; trading on old favor, he grew greedier and more corrupt than ever.

sentences.zh: 大業初，煬帝幸榆林，化及與弟智及違禁與突厥交市。

translations.literal: Early in the Daye reign, when the emperor visited Yulin, Huaji and his brother Zhiji violated the prohibition by trading with the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daye era, when the emperor toured Yulin, Huaji and his brother Zhiji broke the ban on trade with the Turks.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，囚之數月。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and imprisoned them for several months.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and imprisoned them for months.

sentences.zh: 還至青門外，欲斬之而後入城，解衣辮髮，以公主故，久之乃釋，并智及並賜述為奴。

translations.literal: On returning to outside the Green Gate, the emperor wished to behead them before entering the city; their clothes were removed and their hair braided [as condemned men], but because of the princess, after a long time they were released; both Huaji and Zhiji were given to Shu as slaves.
translations.idiomatic: On the return to the capital they were halted outside the Green Gate, where the emperor meant to behead them before entering the city; their robes were stripped and their hair bound like condemned men's, but because of the princess they were held a long while and then spared—both brothers were given to their father Shu as slaves instead.

sentences.zh: 述薨後，煬帝追憶之，遂起化及為右屯衞將軍，智及為將作少監。

translations.literal: After Shu died, the emperor recalled them with fondness and thereupon raised Huaji to General of the Right Tunwei Guard and Zhiji to Vice Director of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu died, the emperor's fond memories returned, and he restored Huaji as general of the Right Tunwei Guard and Zhiji as vice director of palace construction.

sentences.zh: 是時李密據洛口，煬帝懼，留淮左，不敢還都。

translations.literal: At this time Li Mi held Luokou; the emperor was afraid, remained south of the Huai, and did not dare return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi then held Luokou, and the emperor, fearful, lingered south of the Huai and dared not return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 從駕驍果多關中人，久客羈旅，見帝無西意，謀欲叛歸。

translations.literal: Many of the elite guard who accompanied the emperor were men from the Guanzhong region; long guests on the road, seeing that the emperor had no intention of going west, they plotted to rebel and return home.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the emperor's elite guard were men from Guanzhong; weary of long exile on campaign, they saw no sign that the emperor meant to head west again and plotted to desert and return home.

sentences.zh: 時武賁郎將司馬德戡總領驍果，屯於東城，風聞兵士欲叛，未之審，遣校尉元武達陰問驍果，知其情，因謀構逆。

translations.literal: At that time the Martial Guard Gentleman Sima Dekan commanded the elite guard, encamped in the eastern city; he heard on the wind that the soldiers wished to rebel but had not verified it. He sent the company commander Yuan Wuda to inquire secretly among the guard, learned their feelings, and therefore plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The Martial Guard officer Sima Dekan then commanded the elite guard, encamped in the eastern city. Hearing rumors that the troops meant to mutiny but unable to confirm them, he sent company commander Yuan Wuda to sound them out secretly; learning their minds, he began plotting treason.

sentences.zh: 共所善武賁郎將元禮、直閤裴虔通互相扇惑曰：「今聞陛下欲築宮丹陽，勢不還矣。

translations.literal: Together with his close associates, the Martial Guard Gentleman Yuan Li and the Direct Attendant Pei Qiantong, they incited one another, saying: "We now hear that His Majesty wishes to build a palace at Danyang and will certainly not return.
translations.idiomatic: With his confidants Yuan Li, a Martial Guard officer, and Pei Qiantong, a direct attendant, Dekan stirred them up, saying: "We hear His Majesty plans to build a palace at Danyang and will never return west.

sentences.zh: 所部驍果莫不思歸，人人耦語，並謀逃去。

translations.literal: None of the elite guard under command fail to think of returning home; everyone whispers in pairs and together plots to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Every man under our command longs for home; they whisper in pairs and plot to desert together.

sentences.zh: 我欲言之，陛下性忌，惡聞兵走，即恐先事見誅。

translations.literal: If I wish to report this, His Majesty is by nature suspicious and hates to hear of troops fleeing; I fear I would be executed first.
translations.idiomatic: If I report this, His Majesty is suspicious by nature and cannot bear word of troops deserting—we would be executed out of hand.

sentences.zh: 今知而不言，其後事發，又當族滅我矣。

translations.literal: If I know now and do not speak, when the matter breaks later I shall again face extermination of my clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if we know and say nothing, when the plot erupts we shall still face extermination of our clans.

sentences.zh: 進退為戮，將如之何？」

translations.literal: Advance or retreat, we face execution—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Whether we speak or stay silent, we face death—what can we do?"

sentences.zh: 虔通曰：「上實爾，誠為公憂之。」

translations.literal: Pei Qiantong said: "His Majesty is indeed so; I truly worry on your behalf."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Qiantong replied: "That is truly how things stand, and I share your worry."

sentences.zh: 德戡謂兩人曰：「我聞關中陷沒，李孝常以華陰叛，陛下收其二弟，將盡殺之。

translations.literal: Dekan said to the two: "I hear that Guanzhong has fallen, Li Xiaochang rebelled at Huayin, and His Majesty has seized his two younger brothers and intends to kill them all.
translations.idiomatic: Dekan told them both: "I hear Guanzhong has fallen, Li Xiaochang rebelled at Huayin, and His Majesty has seized his two younger brothers and means to execute them all.

sentences.zh: 吾等家屬在西，安得無此慮也！」

translations.literal: Our families are in the west—how can we not have this worry!"
translations.idiomatic: Our kin are still in the west—how can we not fear for them?"

sentences.zh: 虔通曰：「我子弟已壯，誠不自保，正恐旦暮及誅，計無所出。」

translations.literal: Qiantong said: "My sons and younger brothers are already grown; I truly cannot protect myself and fear execution at any moment; I have no plan."
translations.idiomatic: Qiantong said: "My grown sons and brothers are in no safer case—I expect execution at any hour and see no way out."

sentences.zh: 德戡曰：「同相憂，當共為計取。

translations.literal: Dekan said: "Since we share the same worry, we ought together to devise a plan.
translations.idiomatic: Dekan said: "Since we share the same peril, we must plot together.

sentences.zh: 驍果若走，可與俱去。」

translations.literal: If the elite guard flee, we can go with them."
translations.idiomatic: If the guard desert, we can flee with them."

sentences.zh: 虔通等曰：「誠如公言，求生之計，無以易此。」

translations.literal: Qiantong and the others said: "It is truly as you say; for a plan to save our lives, nothing can replace this."
translations.idiomatic: Qiantong and the rest agreed: "You are right—no surer path to survival exists."

sentences.zh: 因遞相招誘。

translations.literal: Thereupon they recruited and enticed one another in turn.
translations.idiomatic: They then recruited one another in turn.

sentences.zh: 又轉告內史舍人元敏、鷹揚郎將孟秉，符璽郎李覆、牛方裕，直長許弘仁、薛良，城門郎唐奉義，醫正張愷等，日夜聚博，約為刎頸之交，情相款昵，言無迴避，於座中輒論叛計，並相然許。

translations.literal: They also passed word to the Secretariat Attendant Yuan Min, the Hawk-raising Gentleman Meng Bing, the Seal and Credential Gentleman Li Fu and Niu Fangyu, the Direct Attendants Xu Hongren and Xue Liang, the Gate Officer Tang Fengyi, the Court Physician Zhang Kai, and others; day and night they gathered to gamble, pledged friendship unto death, were warm and intimate in feeling, spoke without reserve, and at their gatherings openly discussed rebellion—all assented to one another.
translations.idiomatic: Word spread to Secretariat attendant Yuan Min, Hawk-raising officer Meng Bing, seal officers Li Fu and Niu Fangyu, direct attendants Xu Hongren and Xue Liang, gate officer Tang Fengyi, court physician Zhang Kai, and others. Night and day they gambled together, swore blood-brother oaths, grew intimate, spoke without reserve, and openly debated rebellion at the gaming table—all nodding assent.

sentences.zh: 時李孝質在禁，令驍果守之，中外交通，所謀益急。

translations.literal: At that time Li Xiaozhi was in confinement, and the elite guard were ordered to guard him; inside and outside communicated, and the plot grew ever more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiaozhi was then under guard, with elite troops posted around him, so that conspirators within and without could communicate freely and the plot gathered urgency.

sentences.zh: 趙行樞者，樂人之子，家產巨萬，先交智及，勳侍楊士覽者，宇文甥，二人同告智及。

translations.literal: Zhao Xingshu was the son of a musician, his household wealth in the tens of thousands; he had earlier befriended Zhiji. Yang Shilan, an attendant in meritorious service, was a nephew of the Yuwen clan; the two together informed Zhiji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xingshu, son of a court musician and heir to a fortune of tens of thousands, had long been close to Zhiji. Yang Shilan, an attendant in meritorious service and a Yuwen nephew, joined him in telling Zhiji.

sentences.zh: 智及素狂悖，聞之喜，即共見德戡，期以三月十五日舉兵同叛，劫十二衞武馬，虜掠居人財物，結黨西歸。

translations.literal: Zhiji was by nature wild and defiant; hearing this he was pleased and at once went with them to see Dekan. They fixed the fifteenth day of the third month to raise troops and rebel together, seize the war horses of the Twelve Guards, plunder the property of the inhabitants, and form a party to return west.
translations.idiomatic: Wild and reckless by nature, Zhiji was delighted and went at once with them to Dekan. They set the fifteenth day of the third month to rise together, seize the war horses of the Twelve Guards, plunder the townsfolk's goods, and march west in a body.

sentences.zh: 智及曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Zhiji said: "That will not do.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiji objected: "That will not do.

sentences.zh: 當今天實喪隋，英雄並起，同心叛者已數萬人，因行大事，此帝王業也。」

translations.literal: Heaven has truly abandoned Sui; heroes rise together. Those of one mind in rebellion already number in the tens of thousands—by undertaking a great deed, this is the enterprise of an emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has forsaken Sui; heroes rise on every side. Tens of thousands already share our purpose—seize the moment and this becomes an emperor's enterprise."

sentences.zh: 德戡然之。

translations.literal: Dekan assented.
translations.idiomatic: Dekan agreed.

sentences.zh: 行樞、薛良請以化及為主，相約既定，方告化及。

translations.literal: Xingshu and Xue Liang asked to make Huaji their leader; only after the pact was settled did they inform Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshu and Xue Liang proposed making Huaji their leader; only after the pact was sealed did they tell him.

sentences.zh: 化及性本駑怯，初聞大懼，色動流汗，久之乃定。

translations.literal: Huaji's nature was dull and timid; on first hearing he was greatly afraid, his countenance changed and he sweated; only after a long time did he calm.
translations.idiomatic: Dull and timid by nature, Huaji was terrified at first hearing, his face draining of color as sweat poured forth; only after a long while did he steady himself.

sentences.zh: 義寧二年三月一日，德戡欲宣言告眾，恐以人心未一，更思譎詐以脅驍果，謂許弘仁、張愷曰：「君是良醫，國家任使，出言惑眾，眾必信。

translations.literal: On the first day of the third month in the second year of Yining, Dekan wished to proclaim the matter to the masses but feared that hearts were not yet united; he devised further deceit to coerce the elite guard and said to Xu Hongren and Zhang Kai: "You are skilled physicians whom the state employs; if you speak to confuse the masses, they will surely believe.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the third month of the second year of Yining, Dekan wished to announce the plot publicly but feared the troops were not yet of one mind; he devised further deceit to drive the guard and told Xu Hongren and Zhang Kai: "You are trusted physicians in imperial service—your words will sway the men.

sentences.zh: 君可入備身府，告識者，言陛下聞說驍果欲叛，多醞毒酒，因享會盡鴆殺之，獨與南人留此。」

translations.literal: You may enter the Personal Guard office and tell those you know that His Majesty has heard the elite guard wish to rebel, has brewed much poisoned wine, and at a feast will poison them all to death, keeping only the southerners here."
translations.idiomatic: Enter the Personal Guard quarters and spread word that His Majesty has heard the guard mean to rebel, has brewed poisoned wine in quantity, and at the next feast will poison them all, keeping only the southern troops here."

sentences.zh: 弘仁等宣布此言，驍果聞之，遞相告語，謀叛逾急。

translations.literal: Hongren and the others spread this saying; when the elite guard heard it, they told one another in turn, and the plot to rebel grew ever more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Hongren and the rest spread this tale; the guard passed it from man to man, and the conspiracy gathered speed.

sentences.zh: 德戡知計既行，遂以十日總召故人，諭以所為。

translations.literal: Dekan knew the stratagem had taken effect and on the tenth day summoned all his old associates together and instructed them on what was to be done.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his ruse had worked, Dekan on the tenth day summoned all his confederates and laid out the plan.

sentences.zh: 眾皆伏曰：「唯將軍命！」

translations.literal: All bowed and said: "We obey the general's command alone!"
translations.idiomatic: All bowed low: "We await the general's command alone!"

sentences.zh: 其夜，奉義主閉城門，乃與虔通相知，諸門皆不下鑰。

translations.literal: That night Fengyi took charge of closing the city gates; he was in league with Qiantong, and at every gate the locks were not set.
translations.idiomatic: That night Fengyi took charge of the gates in concert with Qiantong, and at every gate the locks were left unset.

sentences.zh: 至夜三更，德戡於東城內集兵，得數萬人，舉火與城外相應。

translations.literal: By the third watch of the night Dekan gathered troops within the eastern city, obtaining several tens of thousands, and raised fires to signal those outside.
translations.idiomatic: By the third watch Dekan had mustered tens of thousands within the eastern city and lit beacon fires to signal allies outside.

sentences.zh: 帝聞有聲，問是何事。

translations.literal: The emperor heard the noise and asked what was happening.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the uproar, the emperor asked what was amiss.

sentences.zh: 虔通偽曰：「草坊被燒，外人救火，故諠囂耳。」

translations.literal: Qiantong falsely said: "The hay storehouse is burning; outsiders are fighting the fire, hence the clamor."
translations.idiomatic: Qiantong lied: "A hay storehouse is afire and men outside are fighting the blaze—that is the noise."

sentences.zh: 中外隔絕，帝以為然。

translations.literal: Inside and outside were cut off from one another; the emperor believed it.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off from the world outside, the emperor believed him.

sentences.zh: 孟秉、智及於城外得千餘人，劫候衞武賁馮普樂，共布兵分捉郭下街巷。

translations.literal: Meng Bing and Zhiji obtained more than a thousand men outside the city, seized the guard officer Feng Pule of the Awaiting Guard, and together deployed troops to seize the lanes and alleys below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the walls Meng Bing and Zhiji rallied more than a thousand men, seized Awaiting Guard officer Feng Pule, and deployed troops to seize the streets below the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 至五更中，德戡授虔通兵，以換諸門衞士。

translations.literal: By the fifth watch Dekan gave troops to Qiantong to replace the gate guards at every gate.
translations.idiomatic: By the fifth watch Dekan handed Qiantong troops to relieve the guards at every gate.

sentences.zh: 虔通因自開門，領數百騎，至成象殿，殺將軍獨孤盛。

translations.literal: Qiantong thereupon opened the gate himself, led several hundred horsemen to the Chengxian Hall, and killed the general Dugu Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qiantong opened the gates himself, led several hundred horsemen to Chengxian Hall, and killed General Dugu Sheng.

sentences.zh: 武賁郎將元禮遂引兵進，宿衞者皆走。

translations.literal: The Martial Guard Gentleman Yuan Li then led troops forward; the night guards all fled.
translations.idiomatic: Martial Guard officer Yuan Li advanced with his men, and the night guards scattered.

sentences.zh: 虔通進兵，排左閤，馳入永巷，問：「陛下安在？」

translations.literal: Qiantong advanced, broke through the left side gate, galloped into the Eternal Lane, and asked: "Where is His Majesty?"
translations.idiomatic: Qiantong pressed forward, broke through the left gate, galloped into the Eternal Lane, and cried: "Where is His Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 有美人出，方指云：「在西閤。」

translations.literal: A palace lady came out and pointed, saying: "In the western pavilion."
translations.idiomatic: A palace lady appeared and pointed: "In the western pavilion."

sentences.zh: 從往執帝。

translations.literal: They went there and seized the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: They went and seized the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝謂虔通曰：「卿非我故人乎！

translations.literal: The emperor said to Qiantong: "Are you not an old acquaintance of mine!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Qiantong: "Are you not an old friend of mine?

sentences.zh: 何恨而反？」

translations.literal: What grudge makes you rebel?"
translations.idiomatic: What grievance drives you to rebel?"

sentences.zh: 虔通曰：「臣不敢反，但將士思歸，奉陛下還京師耳。」

translations.literal: Qiantong said: "Your servant does not dare rebel; only the officers and soldiers long to return home and wish to escort Your Majesty back to the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Qiantong replied: "I dare not rebel, Your Majesty—only the troops long for home and wish to escort you back to the capital."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「與汝歸。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I will return with you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Then return with me."

sentences.zh: 虔通因勒兵守之。

translations.literal: Qiantong thereupon deployed troops to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: Qiantong deployed troops to hold him under guard.

sentences.zh: 至旦，孟秉以甲騎迎化及。

translations.literal: At dawn Meng Bing met Huaji with armored cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Meng Bing rode out in armor to welcome Huaji.

sentences.zh: 化及未知事果，戰慄不能言，人有來謁之者，但低頭據鞍，答云「罪過」。

translations.literal: Huaji did not yet know how the affair had turned out; he trembled and could not speak. When someone came to pay respects, he only bowed his head on the saddle and answered "My fault."
translations.idiomatic: Huaji still did not know the coup had succeeded; he trembled speechless on his saddle, and when men came to salute him he only bowed his head and muttered "My fault."

sentences.zh: 時士及在公主第，弗之知也。

translations.literal: At that time Shiji was at the princess's residence and knew nothing of it.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji was then at the princess's mansion and knew nothing of events.

sentences.zh: 智及遣家僮莊桃樹就第殺之，桃樹不忍，執詣智及，久之乃見釋。

translations.literal: Zhiji sent the household slave Zhuang Taoshu to the residence to kill him; Taoshu could not bear to do it, seized Shiji and brought him to Zhiji, and only after a long time was he released.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiji sent his servant Zhuang Taoshu to kill him at the mansion; Taoshu could not bring himself to strike, seized Shiji instead, and brought him to Zhiji, who held him a long while before sparing him.

sentences.zh: 化及至城門，德戡迎謁，引入朝堂，號為丞相。

translations.literal: When Huaji reached the city gate, Dekan met and paid homage to him, led him into the audience hall, and styled him Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji reached the gate, Dekan met him with obeisance, led him to the audience hall, and proclaimed him Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 令將帝出江都門以示羣賊，因復將入。

translations.literal: He ordered the emperor brought out through the Jiangdu Gate to show him to the rebel masses, then brought him back in again.
translations.idiomatic: He had the emperor paraded outside the Jiangdu Gate to display him to the rebel host, then brought him back within.

sentences.zh: 遣令狐行達弒帝於宮中，又執朝臣不同己者數十人及諸外戚，無少長害之，唯留秦孝王子浩，立以為帝。

translations.literal: He sent Linghu Xingda to assassinate the emperor within the palace; he also seized several tens of court ministers who did not agree with him and various imperial affines, killing them without regard to age, sparing only Prince Hao, son of Emperor Xiaojing of Qin, whom he set up as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Linghu Xingda to murder the emperor in the palace, seized dozens of courtiers who opposed him along with numerous imperial affines, and slaughtered them without regard to age, sparing only Prince Hao, son of Emperor Xiaojing of Qin, whom he enthroned as puppet emperor.

sentences.zh: 十餘日，奪江都人舟楫，從水路西歸。

translations.literal: After more than ten days he seized the boats of the people of Jiangdu and returned west by water.
translations.idiomatic: Within a fortnight he seized the boats of Jiangdu's people and set out westward by water.

sentences.zh: 至顯福宮，宿公麥孟才、折衝郎將沈光等謀擊化及，反為所害。

translations.literal: At Xianfu Palace, the Household Steward Mai Mengcai, the Shock-Campaign Gentleman Shen Guang, and others plotted to strike Huaji but were instead killed by him.
translations.idiomatic: At Xianfu Palace, household steward Mai Mengcai, shock-campaign officer Shen Guang, and others plotted to strike Huaji down but were themselves killed.

sentences.zh: 化及於是入據六宮，其自奉養一如煬帝故事。

translations.literal: Huaji thereupon entered and occupied the six palaces; his own maintenance followed the emperor Yang's precedent in every respect.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji then seized the six palaces and maintained himself in every way as Emperor Yang had done.

sentences.zh: 每於帳中南面端坐，人有白事者，默然不對。

translations.literal: Each day he sat facing south within his tent; when someone reported affairs, he remained silent and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he sat facing south within his tent; when petitioners came he answered not a word.

sentences.zh: 下牙時，方收取啟狀，共奉義、方裕、良、愷等參決之。

translations.literal: Only when court was dismissed did he gather memorials; Fengyi, Fangyu, Liang, Kai, and others jointly decided them.
translations.idiomatic: Only when court ended did he gather memorials for Fengyi, Fangyu, Liang, Kai, and the rest to decide jointly.

sentences.zh: 行至徐州，水路不通，復奪人車牛，得二千兩，並載宮人珍寶。

translations.literal: When they reached Xuzhou the waterways were blocked; he again seized people's carts and oxen, obtaining two thousand teams, and loaded palace women and precious goods upon them.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuzhou the waterways were blocked, so he seized carts and oxen from the populace—two thousand teams in all—and loaded palace women and treasure aboard.

sentences.zh: 其戈甲戎器，悉令軍士負之。

translations.literal: All weapons and armor he ordered the soldiers to carry on their backs.
translations.idiomatic: Weapons and armor he made the soldiers carry on their backs.

sentences.zh: 道遠疲極，三軍始怨。

translations.literal: The road was long and exhaustion extreme; the three armies began to murmur in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The march was long and exhaustion extreme; the army began to murmur.

sentences.zh: 德戡失望，竊謂行樞曰：「君大謬誤我。

translations.literal: Dekan was disappointed and said privately to Xingshu: "You have gravely misled me.
translations.idiomatic: Dekan, bitterly disappointed, whispered to Xingshu: "You misled me badly.

sentences.zh: 當今撥亂，必藉英賢，化及庸暗，羣小在側，事將必敗，當若之何？」

translations.literal: To settle chaos today one must rely on heroic worthies; Huaji is mediocre and dim, petty men are at his side, affairs will surely fail—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: To restore order one needs a true hero; Huaji is dull and petty men swarm about him—the enterprise must fail. What can we do?"

sentences.zh: 行樞曰：「在我等爾，廢之何難！」

translations.literal: Xingshu said: "It rests with us—how hard is it to depose him!"
translations.idiomatic: Xingshu replied: "That rests with us—how hard is it to depose him?"

sentences.zh: 因共李本、宇文導師、尹正卿等謀，以後軍萬餘兵襲殺化及，更立德戡為主。

translations.literal: Thereupon together with Li Ben, Yuwen Daoshi, Yin Zhengqing, and others they plotted to use more than ten thousand rear-guard troops to surprise and kill Huaji and set up Dekan as leader instead.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Li Ben, Yuwen Daoshi, Yin Zhengqing, and others they plotted to use the rear guard—more than ten thousand men—to surprise and kill Huaji and make Dekan leader instead.

sentences.zh: 弘仁知之，密告化及，盡收捕德戡及其支黨十餘人，皆殺之。

translations.literal: Hongren learned of it and secretly informed Huaji; all of Dekan and his faction of more than ten were seized and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Hongren learned of the plot and secretly informed Huaji, who seized Dekan and more than ten of his faction and executed them all.

sentences.zh: 引兵向東郡，通守王軌以城降之。

translations.literal: He led troops toward Dongjun; the transit intendant Wang Gui surrendered the city to him.
translations.idiomatic: He marched toward Dong Commandery, where transit intendant Wang Gui surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 元文都推越王侗為主，拜李密為太尉，令擊化及。

translations.literal: Yuan Wendu installed Prince Yue Tong as ruler, appointed Li Mi Grand Marshal, and ordered him to attack Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Wendu enthroned Prince Yue Tong and appointed Li Mi Grand Marshal with orders to attack Huaji.

sentences.zh: 密遣徐勣據黎陽倉。

translations.literal: Li Mi sent Xu Jixing to hold Liyang granary.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi sent Xu Jixing to hold the Liyang granary.

sentences.zh: 化及渡河，保黎陽縣，分兵圍勣。

translations.literal: Huaji crossed the river, held Liyang county, and divided troops to besiege Jixing.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji crossed the river, fortified Liyang county, and sent detachments to besiege Jixing.

sentences.zh: 密壁清淇，與勣以烽火相應。

translations.literal: Li Mi fortified at Qingqi and coordinated with Jixing by beacon fires.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi fortified at Qingqi and coordinated with Jixing by beacon fire.

sentences.zh: 化及每攻倉，密輒引兵救之。

translations.literal: Whenever Huaji attacked the granary, Li Mi at once led troops to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Huaji attacked the granary, Li Mi marched to its relief.

sentences.zh: 化及數戰不利，其將軍于弘達為密所擒，送於侗所，鑊烹之。

translations.literal: Huaji fought several times without success; his general Yu Hongda was captured by Li Mi, sent to Tong's court, and boiled alive in a cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji lost battle after battle; his general Yu Hongda was captured by Li Mi, sent to Prince Tong's court, and boiled alive in a cauldron.

sentences.zh: 化及糧盡，渡永濟渠，與密決戰於童山，遂入汲郡求軍糧，又遣使拷掠東郡吏民以責米粟。

translations.literal: When Huaji's grain was exhausted, he crossed the Yongji Canal and fought a decisive battle with Li Mi at Tongshan, then entered Ji commandery to seek army grain, and again sent envoys to torture and plunder the officials and people of Dong commandery to demand rice and grain.
translations.idiomatic: With supplies exhausted, Huaji crossed the Yongji Canal and fought Li Mi in a decisive battle at Tongshan, then entered Ji Commandery for provisions and sent agents to torture officials and commoners in Dong Commandery for grain.

sentences.zh: 王軌怨之，以城歸於李密。

translations.literal: Wang Gui resented this and surrendered the city to Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui, resentful, surrendered the city to Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 化及大懼，自汲郡將率眾圖以北諸州。

translations.literal: Huaji was greatly afraid and from Ji commandery intended to lead his masses to seize the northern provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Huaji planned to march north from Ji Commandery and seize the northern provinces.

sentences.zh: 其將陳智略率嶺南驍果萬餘人，張童兒率江東驍果數千人，皆叛歸李密。

translations.literal: His generals Chen Zhilüe led more than ten thousand elite guard from Lingnan, and Zhang Tong'er led several thousand elite guard from Jiangdong—all rebelled and returned to Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: General Chen Zhilüe led more than ten thousand Lingnan elite troops and Zhang Tong'er several thousand Jiangdong elite troops—all deserted to Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 化及尚有眾二萬，北走魏縣。

translations.literal: Huaji still had twenty thousand followers and fled north to Wei county.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji still had twenty thousand men and fled north to Wei county.

sentences.zh: 張愷等與其將陳伯謀去之，事覺，為化及所殺。

translations.literal: Zhang Kai and his general Chen Bomou wished to leave him; when the affair was discovered, Huaji killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kai and his general Chen Bomou tried to desert; discovered, they were executed by Huaji.

sentences.zh: 腹心稍盡，兵勢日蹙，兄弟更無他計，但相聚酣宴，奏女樂。

translations.literal: His close confidants were gradually exhausted, military strength daily pressed; the brothers had no other plan but to gather for feasting and female music.
translations.idiomatic: His inner circle dwindled and his forces shrank daily; the brothers could do nothing but feast together to female music.

sentences.zh: 醉後，因尤智及曰：「我初不知，由汝為計，強來立我。

translations.literal: When drunk, he blamed Zhiji, saying: "At first I did not know; it was your plan that forced me to be set up.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, he blamed Zhiji: "I never wanted this—you forced the crown on me.

sentences.zh: 今所向無成，士馬日散，負殺主之名，天下所不納。

translations.literal: Now nothing succeeds, troops and horses daily scatter; bearing the name of regicide, the world will not accept us.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing succeeds, our forces scatter daily, we bear the name of regicides, and the world rejects us.

sentences.zh: 今者滅族，豈不由汝乎？」

translations.literal: Now our clan faces extinction—is it not because of you?
translations.idiomatic: Our clan faces extinction—is it not your fault?"

sentences.zh: 持其兩子而泣。

translations.literal: He seized his two sons and wept.
translations.idiomatic: He seized his two sons and wept.

sentences.zh: 智及怒曰：「事捷之日，都不賜尤，及其將敗，乃欲歸罪。

translations.literal: Zhiji angrily said: "When affairs succeeded, you never blamed me; now that defeat approaches, you wish to shift guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiji snapped: "When we won you never blamed me; now we lose, you shift the blame.

sentences.zh: 何不殺我以降建德？」

translations.literal: Why not kill me and surrender to Jiande?
translations.idiomatic: Why not kill me and surrender to Dou Jiande?"

sentences.zh: 兄弟數相鬬鬩，言無長幼，醒而復飲，以此為恒。

translations.literal: The brothers repeatedly brawled, speaking without regard for seniority; sobering they drank again—this became their constant pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers brawled repeatedly without regard for rank, sobered, drank again—this became their routine.

sentences.zh: 其眾多亡，自知必敗，化及歎曰：「人生故當死，豈不一日為帝乎？」

translations.literal: Many of his followers fled; knowing he must fail, Huaji sighed: "A man is born to die—was it not worth being emperor for a single day?"
translations.idiomatic: As his men deserted and defeat loomed, Huaji sighed: "Man is born to die—was one day as emperor not worth it?"

sentences.zh: 於是鴆殺浩，僭皇帝位於魏縣，國號許，建元為天壽，署置百官。

translations.literal: Thereupon he poisoned Hao, usurped the imperial title at Wei county, named the state Xu, established the era name Tianshou, and appointed the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: He poisoned Hao, declared himself emperor at Wei county, named his state Xu, adopted the era name Tianshou, and appointed officials.

sentences.zh: 攻元寶藏於魏州，四旬不剋，反為所敗，亡失千餘人。

translations.literal: He attacked Yuan Baocang at Weizhou; after forty days he could not take it and was instead defeated, losing more than a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Yuan Baocang at Weizhou; after forty days without success he was defeated and lost more than a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 乃東北趣聊城，將招攜海曲諸賊。

translations.literal: He then turned northeast toward Liaocheng, intending to recruit the bandits along the coast.
translations.idiomatic: He marched northeast toward Liaocheng to recruit coastal bandits.

sentences.zh: 時遣士及徇濟北，求餽餉。

translations.literal: At that time he sent Shiji to pacify Jibei and seek provisions.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Shiji to scour Jibei for supplies.

sentences.zh: 大唐遣淮安王神通安撫山東，并招化及。

translations.literal: The Great Tang sent Prince Huai'an Li Shentong to pacify Shandong and also summon Huaji to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Tang sent Prince Huai'an Li Shentong to pacify Shandong and summon Huaji to submit.

sentences.zh: 化及不從，神通進兵圍之，十餘日不剋而退。

translations.literal: Huaji refused; Shentong advanced to besiege him but after more than ten days could not take the city and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji refused; Shentong besieged him over ten days without success and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 竇建德悉眾攻之。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande attacked with his full force.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande attacked with his entire army.

sentences.zh: 先是，齊州賊帥王薄聞其多寶物，詐來投附。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Qi bandit chief Wang Bo heard Huaji had many treasures and falsely came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Qi bandit Wang Bo, hearing of Huaji's treasure, feigned submission.

sentences.zh: 化及信之，與共居守。

translations.literal: Huaji trusted him and had him jointly guard the city.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji trusted him and made him co-defender of the city.

sentences.zh: 至是，薄引建德入城，生擒化及，悉虜其眾。

translations.literal: At this time Bo led Jiande's troops into the city and captured Huaji alive, taking all his followers captive.
translations.idiomatic: Bo then admitted Jiande's troops, captured Huaji alive, and seized his entire force.

sentences.zh: 先執智及、元武達、孟秉、楊士覽、許弘仁，皆斬之。

translations.literal: First they seized Zhiji, Yuan Wuda, Meng Bing, Yang Shilan, and Xu Hongren—all were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiji, Yuan Wuda, Meng Bing, Yang Shilan, and Xu Hongren were seized first and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 乃以轞車載化及之河間，數以殺君之罪，并二子承基、承趾皆斬之，傳首於突厥義成公主，梟於虜庭。

translations.literal: Then they loaded Huaji on a caged cart to Hejian, repeatedly charged him with the crime of killing his sovereign, and beheaded him together with his two sons Chenggi and Chengzhi; their heads were sent to Princess Yicheng of the Turks and displayed in the barbarian court.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji was carted to Hejian, charged repeatedly with regicide, and beheaded with his sons Chenggi and Chengzhi; their heads were sent to the Turkic Princess Yicheng and displayed on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 士及自濟北西歸長安。

translations.literal: Shiji returned from Jibei westward to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji returned from Jibei to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 智及幼頑凶，好與人羣鬬，所共遊處，皆不逞之徒，相聚鬬雞，習放鷹狗。

translations.literal: From youth Zhiji was violent and fierce, fond of brawling in groups; those with whom he associated were all unruly men, gathering to fight cocks and practice hawking and dog-running.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiji was violent from youth, brawling constantly with unruly companions who cockfought and hunted with hawks and dogs.

sentences.zh: 初以父功，賜爵濮陽郡公。

translations.literal: Initially because of his father's merit he was granted the title Duke of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: For his father's merit he was made Duke of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 蒸淫醜穢，無所不為。

translations.literal: Incestuous debauchery and filth—there was nothing he would not do.
translations.idiomatic: He committed every sort of incest and debauchery.

sentences.zh: 其妻長孫，妬而告述，述雖為隱，而大忿之，纖芥之愆，必加鞭箠。

translations.literal: His wife of the Zhangsun clan, jealous, reported him to Shu; Shu concealed it but was greatly angered, and for the slightest fault he was sure to be flogged.
translations.idiomatic: His jealous wife Zhangsun reported him to Shu, who concealed the matter but flogged him for the slightest fault.

sentences.zh: 弟士及恃尚主，又輕忽之。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shiji relied on marriage to a princess and also treated him lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Shiji, backed by a princess marriage, treated him with contempt.

sentences.zh: 唯化及每事營護，父再三欲殺，輒救免之，由是頗相親昵。

translations.literal: Only Huaji protected him in every matter; the father several times wished to kill him but Huaji always saved him, and therefore they were rather intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Only Huaji shielded him; Shu several times meant to kill him but Huaji always intervened, and they grew close.

sentences.zh: 遂勸化及遣人入蕃，私為交易。

translations.literal: Zhiji therefore urged Huaji to send men into the frontier tribes to trade privately.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiji persuaded Huaji to send men for illicit frontier trade.

sentences.zh: 事發，當誅，述獨證智及罪惡，而為化及請命。

translations.literal: When the affair broke, they should have been executed; Shu alone testified to Zhiji's crimes and pleaded for Huaji's life.
translations.idiomatic: When discovered they faced execution; Shu testified only against Zhiji and pleaded for Huaji.

sentences.zh: 帝因兩釋。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore released both.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor spared them both.

sentences.zh: 述將死，抗表言其凶勃，必且破家。

translations.literal: When Shu was dying, he submitted a memorial stating Zhiji's violence and that he would surely destroy the family.
translations.idiomatic: Dying, Shu memorialized that Zhiji's violence would destroy the clan.

sentences.zh: 帝後思述，授智及將作少監。

translations.literal: The emperor later recalled Shu and appointed Zhiji Vice Director of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor later recalled Shu and made Zhiji vice director of palace construction.

sentences.zh: 其江都殺逆之事，智及之謀也。

translations.literal: The Jiangdu regicide was Zhiji's plot.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangdu regicide was Zhiji's doing.

sentences.zh: 化及為丞相，以為左僕射，領十二衞大將軍。

translations.literal: When Huaji became Chancellor, he was made Left Vice Minister and General-in-Chief of the Twelve Guards.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor Huaji made him left vice minister and general of the Twelve Guards.

sentences.zh: 化及僭號，封齊王。

translations.literal: When Huaji usurped the throne, he was enfeoffed Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji declared himself emperor, Zhiji was made Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 竇建德破聊城，獲而斬之，并其黨十餘人，皆暴屍梟首。

translations.literal: When Jiande took Liaocheng he captured and beheaded him, and more than ten of his faction were exposed with corpses and heads displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande captured and beheaded him at Liaocheng, exposing more than ten of his faction.

sentences.zh: 司馬德戡，扶風雍人也。

translations.literal: Sima Dekan—Sima Dekan was a man of Yong in Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Dekan was a native of Yong in Fufeng commandery.

sentences.zh: 父元謙，仕周為都督。

translations.literal: His father Yuanqian served Zhou as a commander.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuanqian served as a Zhou commander.

sentences.zh: 德戡幼孤，以屠豕自給。

translations.literal: Dekan was orphaned young and supported himself by butchering pigs.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Dekan butchered pigs for a living.

sentences.zh: 有桑門釋粲，通德戡母和氏，遂撫教之，因解書計。

translations.literal: There was a Buddhist monk Shi Can who knew Dekan's mother Lady He and came to nurture and teach him, whereupon he learned writing and reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Monk Shi Can knew his mother Lady He, raised and taught him, and he learned writing and reckoning.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，為侍官，漸遷至大都督。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era he became an attendant officer and was gradually promoted to Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kaihuang he became an attendant officer and rose to grand commander.

sentences.zh: 從楊素出討漢王諒，充內營左右，進止便僻，俊辯多姦計，素大善之。

translations.literal: Following Yang Su on the campaign against Prince Han Liang, he served in the inner camp as left and right attendant; his comings and goings were convenient and agreeable, he was eloquent with many crafty schemes, and Su greatly favored him.
translations.idiomatic: On Yang Su's campaign against Prince Han Liang he served in the inner camp, was nimble and eloquent with many schemes, and Su favored him greatly.

sentences.zh: 以勳授儀同三司。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted the title of Honored Companion, Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he received the title Honored Companion, Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 大業三年，為鷹揚郎將。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daye he became Hawk-raising Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye year three he became hawk-raising gentleman.

sentences.zh: 從討遼左，進位正議大夫，遷武賁郎將。

translations.literal: Following the Liaodong campaign, he was promoted to Correct Counselor and transferred to Martial Guard Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: On the Liaodong campaign he rose to correct counselor and martial guard gentleman.

sentences.zh: 煬帝甚昵之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang was very intimate with him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor doted on him.

sentences.zh: 從至江都，領左右備身驍果萬人，營於城內。

translations.literal: Following the emperor to Jiangdu, he commanded ten thousand elite Personal Guard troops encamped within the city.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangdu he commanded ten thousand elite personal guards within the city.

sentences.zh: 因隋末大亂，乃率驍果謀反，語在化及事中。

translations.literal: Because of the great chaos at the end of Sui, he led the elite guard in rebellion, as told in Huaji's biography.
translations.idiomatic: In the Sui collapse he led the guard in rebellion, as told in Huaji's account.

sentences.zh: 既獲煬帝，與其黨孟秉等推化及為丞相。

translations.literal: After seizing the emperor, he and his faction Meng Bing and others installed Huaji as Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: After seizing the emperor he and Meng Bing's faction made Huaji chancellor.

sentences.zh: 化及首封德戡為溫國公，邑三千戶，加光祿大夫，仍統本兵。

translations.literal: Huaji first enfeoffed Dekan as Duke of Wen with three thousand households, added Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and still commanded his original troops.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji first made him Duke of Wen, three thousand households, grand master for splendid happiness, still commanding his troops.

sentences.zh: 化及意甚忌之。

translations.literal: Huaji was very jealous of him.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji deeply mistrusted him.

sentences.zh: 後數日，化及署諸將，分配士卒，乃以德戡為禮部尚書，外示美遷，實奪其兵也。

translations.literal: Several days later Huaji assigned the various generals and distributed troops, then made Dekan Minister of Rites—a fine promotion outwardly but in fact stripping his soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Huaji reassigned troops and made Dekan minister of rites—ostensibly promotion, in fact stripping his command.

sentences.zh: 由是憤怨，所獲賞物皆賂於智及，智及為之言。

translations.literal: Because of this he was resentful and bribed Zhiji with all rewards received; Zhiji spoke on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Resentful, he bribed Zhiji with every reward; Zhiji pleaded for him.

sentences.zh: 行至徐州，捨舟登陸，令德戡將後軍，乃與趙行樞、李本、尹正卿、宇文導師等謀襲化及，遣人使于孟海公，結為外助。

translations.literal: Reaching Xuzhou they left the boats and went ashore; Huaji ordered Dekan to command the rear guard, and together with Zhao Xingshu, Li Ben, Yin Zhengqing, Yuwen Daoshi, and others plotted to surprise Huaji, sending men to Meng Haigong to ally as external aid.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuzhou they disembarked; Huaji put Dekan in the rear guard while he plotted with Zhao Xingshu, Li Ben, Yin Zhengqing, Yuwen Daoshi, and others to strike Huaji and sent envoys to Meng Haigong for aid.

sentences.zh: 遷延未發，以待使報。

translations.literal: They delayed and did not act, waiting for the envoy's reply.
translations.idiomatic: They delayed, awaiting the envoy's reply.

sentences.zh: 許弘仁、張愷知之，以告化及，因遣其弟士及陽為遊獵，至于後軍。

translations.literal: Xu Hongren and Zhang Kai learned of it and informed Huaji; Huaji therefore sent his younger brother Shiji under pretense of hunting to the rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: Hongren and Zhang Kai informed Huaji, who sent Shiji hunting toward the rear guard.

sentences.zh: 德戡不知事露，出營參謁，因命執之，并其黨與。

translations.literal: Dekan did not know the affair was exposed; he left camp to pay respects and was seized together with his faction.
translations.idiomatic: Unaware, Dekan left camp to pay respects and was seized with his faction.

sentences.zh: 化及責之曰：「與公戮力共定海內，出於萬死。

translations.literal: Huaji reproached him: "With you I shared hardship and together settled the realm, emerging from ten thousand deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji reproached him: "We survived ten thousand deaths together to settle the realm.

sentences.zh: 今始事成，願得同守富貴，公又何為反也？」

translations.literal: Now affairs have just succeeded and I wish to share wealth with you—why do you rebel?
translations.idiomatic: Success is at hand and I wished to share wealth—why rebel?"

sentences.zh: 德戡曰：「本殺昏主，苦其毒害。

translations.literal: Dekan said: "Originally we killed the benighted sovereign because we suffered his poison.
translations.idiomatic: Dekan said: "We killed the tyrant because we suffered his cruelty.

sentences.zh: 推立足下，而又甚之。

translations.literal: We set you up, yet you surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: We made you leader, yet you surpassed him.

sentences.zh: 逼於物情，不獲已也。」

translations.literal: Pressed by circumstance, I had no choice."
translations.idiomatic: Circumstance left me no choice."

sentences.zh: 化及不對，命送至幕下，縊而殺之，時年三十九。

translations.literal: Huaji did not reply and ordered him sent below the tent, strangled and killed; he was thirty-nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji said nothing, had him strangled below the tent; he was thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 裴虔通，河東人也。

translations.literal: Pei Qiantong—Pei Qiantong was a man of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Qiantong was from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 初，煬帝為晉王，以親信從，稍遷至監門校尉。

translations.literal: Initially when Yang Guang was Prince of Jin he followed as a trusted intimate and was gradually promoted to Gate Guard company commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Guang was Prince of Jin, Qiantong served as trusted intimate and rose to gate guard company commander.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，擢舊左右，授宣惠尉，遷監門直閤。

translations.literal: When Yang Guang took the throne he promoted his old intimates, appointing him Xuanhui Captain and transferring him to Direct Attendant of the Gate Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On accession he promoted old intimates, making Qiantong Xuanhui captain then direct gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 累從征役，至通議大夫。

translations.literal: He repeatedly followed campaigns until he reached General for Promoting Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned repeatedly to general for promoting justice.

sentences.zh: 與司馬德戡同謀作亂，先開宮門，騎至成象殿，殺將軍獨孤盛，擒帝于西閤。

translations.literal: Plotting rebellion together with Sima Dekan, he first opened the palace gates, rode to Chengxian Hall, killed General Dugu Sheng, and seized the emperor in the western pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: With Dekan he opened the gates, rode to Chengxian Hall, killed Dugu Sheng, and seized the emperor in the western pavilion.

sentences.zh: 化及以虔通為光祿大夫、莒國公。

translations.literal: Huaji made Qiantong Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Duke of Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji made him grand master for splendid happiness and Duke of Ju.

sentences.zh: 化及引兵之北也，令鎮徐州。

translations.literal: When Huaji led troops north he ordered him to garrison Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji marched north he garrisoned Qiantong at Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 化及敗後，歸於大唐，即授徐州總管，轉辰州刺史，封長蛇男。

translations.literal: After Huaji's defeat he submitted to the Great Tang and was at once appointed Xuzhou regional commander, then transferred to Chen prefect and enfeoffed Baron of Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: After Huaji's defeat he submitted to Tang, became Xuzhou regional commander, then Chen prefect and Baron of Changshe.

sentences.zh: 尋以隋朝殺逆之罪，除名，徙於嶺表而死。

translations.literal: Soon because of the crime of regicide in Sui he was stripped of name and banished to the southern marches, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon stripped for Sui regicide and banished to the south, where he died.

sentences.zh: 王充字行滿，本西域人也。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong—Wang Shichong, style Xingman, was originally from the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong, style Xingman, was of Western Regions origin.

sentences.zh: 祖支頹䅶，徙居新豐。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhi Niantu moved to Xinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhi Niantu settled in Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 頹䅶死，其妻少寡，與儀同王粲野合，生子曰瓊，粲遂納之以為小妻。

translations.literal: When Niantu died his wife was young and widowed; she had illicit relations with the Honored Companion Wang Can in the wild and bore a son named Qiong; Can then took her in as a concubine.
translations.idiomatic: After Niantu died his young widow lay with Honored Companion Wang Can and bore Qiong; Can took her as concubine.

sentences.zh: 其父收幼孤，隨母嫁粲，粲愛而養之，因姓王氏，官至懷、汴二州長史。

translations.literal: Shichong's father took in the young orphan; following his mother's remarriage to Can, Can loved and raised him, and therefore he took the surname Wang, rising to prefect of Huai and Bian prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong's father was raised by Can after the remarriage; Shichong took the Wang surname and his father became prefect of Huai and Bian.

sentences.zh: 充捲髮豺聲，沉猜多詭詐，頗窺書傳，尤好兵法，曉龜策推步盈虛，然未嘗為人言也。

translations.literal: Shichong had curly hair and a jackal's voice, was deep, suspicious, and full of crafty deceit; he pored over books, especially loved military strategy, and understood tortoise divination and calendrical calculation, yet never spoke of these to others.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong had curly hair and a harsh voice, was secretive and cunning, studied books especially military arts and divination, yet never spoke of them.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，為左翊衞，後以軍功拜儀同，授兵部員外。

translations.literal: In Kaihuang he served in the Left Yiwu Guard; later for military merit he was made Honored Companion and given the post of Vice Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kaihuang he served the Left Yiwu Guard; for merit he became honored companion and war ministry vice director.

sentences.zh: 善敷奏，明習法律，而舞弄文墨，高下其心。

translations.literal: He was skilled at memorials and understood law, yet manipulated documents and bent the law to his will.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted memorials expertly and knew law, yet twisted documents to his will.

sentences.zh: 或有駁難之者，充利口飾非，辭義鋒起，眾雖知其不可而莫能屈，稱為明辯。

translations.literal: When someone refuted him, Shichong with sharp tongue glossed over wrongs and arguments flashed forth; though all knew he was wrong none could overcome him, and he was called clear in debate.
translations.idiomatic: When challenged he argued brilliantly; though all knew him wrong none could best him, and he was called a master debater.

sentences.zh: 煬帝時，累遷至江都郡丞。

translations.literal: In the Yang emperor's time he was repeatedly promoted to Jiangdu commandery assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yang he rose to Jiangdu commandery assistant.

sentences.zh: 時帝數幸江都，充善候人主顏色，阿諛順旨，每入言事，帝善之。

translations.literal: The emperor often visited Jiangdu; Shichong was skilled at reading his mood, flattering and following his wishes; whenever he entered to speak the emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often visited Jiangdu; Shichong read his mood, flattered him, and pleased him whenever he spoke.

sentences.zh: 又以郡丞領江都宮監，乃雕飾池臺，陰奏遠方珍物以媚於帝，由是益昵之。

translations.literal: Also as commandery assistant he oversaw the Jiangdu palace; he carved and adorned pools and terraces and secretly memorialized exotic goods from distant regions to please the emperor, and therefore grew even more intimate.
translations.idiomatic: As assistant he oversaw the palace, adorned pools and terraces, and sent exotic tribute to win greater favor.

sentences.zh: 大業八年，隋始亂，充內懷徼倖，卑身禮士，陰結豪俊，多收眾心。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Daye, as Sui began to collapse, Shichong inwardly hoped for fortune, humbled himself to honor scholars, secretly joined bold heroes, and widely won hearts.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye year eight, as Sui collapsed, Shichong courted scholars, rallied heroes, and won popular hearts.

sentences.zh: 江淮間人素輕悍，又屬盜賊羣起，人多犯法，有繫獄抵罪者，充皆枉法出之，以樹私恩。

translations.literal: The people between the Yangtze and Huai were by nature light and fierce; moreover bandits rose everywhere and many broke the law; those imprisoned for crimes Shichong released by bending the law to build private favor.
translations.idiomatic: Between Yangtze and Huai the people were fierce; as bandits rose he illegally freed prisoners to buy loyalty.

sentences.zh: 及楊玄感反，吳人朱爕、晉陵人管崇起兵江南以應之，自稱將軍，擁眾十餘萬。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, the Wu man Zhu Fen and Jingling man Guan Chong raised troops in Jiangnan in response, styled themselves generals, and mustered more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, Zhu Fen of Wu and Guan Chong of Jingling raised a hundred thousand in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 帝遣將軍吐萬緒、魚俱羅討之，不能剋。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Generals Tuwan Xu and Yu Juluo to attack them but could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Tuwan Xu and Yu Juluo failed to defeat them.

sentences.zh: 充募江都萬餘人，擊頻破之。

translations.literal: Shichong recruited more than ten thousand from Jiangdu and repeatedly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong recruited ten thousand Jiangdu men and repeatedly defeated them.

sentences.zh: 每有剋捷，必歸功於下，所獲軍實，皆推與士卒，身無所受。

translations.literal: Whenever he won he always attributed merit to subordinates and gave captured military goods entirely to the soldiers, taking none himself.
translations.idiomatic: He credited subordinates with every victory and gave all booty to the troops, keeping none.

sentences.zh: 由此人爭為用，功最居多。

translations.literal: Therefore men vied to serve him and his achievements were greatest.
translations.idiomatic: Men flocked to him and his achievements topped all others.

sentences.zh: 十年，齊郡賊帥孟讓自長白山寇掠諸郡，至盱眙，有眾十餘萬。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Qi bandit chief Meng Rang raided the commanderies from Changbai Mountain to Xuyi with more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In year ten, Meng Rang of Qi raided from Changbai to Xuyi with a hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 充以兵拒之，而羸師示弱，保都梁山為五柵，相持不戰。

translations.literal: Shichong resisted with troops but showed a weak force, held Mount Duliang in five palisades, and faced off without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong met him with a feigned weak force, fortified Mount Duliang in five camps, and held without battle.

sentences.zh: 後因其懈弛，出兵奮擊，大破之，乘勝盡滅賊，讓以數十騎遁去，斬首萬人，六畜、軍資莫不盡獲。

translations.literal: Later when the enemy relaxed he sent troops in a fierce assault, routed them utterly, pursued to destroy the bandits; Rang fled with several dozen horsemen; ten thousand heads were cut off and livestock and military goods were all captured.
translations.idiomatic: When they relaxed he struck fiercely, destroyed them utterly; Rang fled with dozens of horsemen; ten thousand heads fell and all livestock and supplies were seized.

sentences.zh: 帝以充有將帥才略，始遣領兵，討諸小盜，所向皆破之。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering Shichong had talent and strategy as a commander, first sent him to lead troops against the minor bandits; wherever he went he broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Shichong's military talent, the emperor first sent him against minor bandits and he broke them wherever he marched.

sentences.zh: 然性矯偽，詐為善，能自勤苦，以求聲譽。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was hypocritical and false; he pretended goodness and could impose hardship on himself to seek reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was a hypocrite who played at virtue and wore hardship to win reputation.

sentences.zh: 十一年，突厥圍帝於雁門，充盡發江都人，將往赴難。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Turks besieged the emperor at Yanmen; Shichong mobilized all the people of Jiangdu to go to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven, when Turks besieged the emperor at Yanmen, Shichong mobilized all Jiangdu to march to his relief.

sentences.zh: 在軍中，反首垢面，悲泣無度，曉夜不解甲，藉草而臥。

translations.literal: In the army he turned his head and smeared his face with dirt, wept beyond measure, did not remove his armor day or night, and slept on straw.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign he smeared his face, wept endlessly, slept in armor on straw day and night.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，以為愛己，益信任之。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this he thought Shichong loved him and trusted him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took this as devotion and trusted him more than ever.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遷為江都通守。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to Jiangdu transit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve he became Jiangdu transit intendant.

sentences.zh: 時厭次人格謙為盜數年，兵十餘萬，在豆子䴚中。

translations.literal: At that time Ge Qian of Yanci had been a bandit for years with more than a hundred thousand troops in Douzi Dam.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit Ge Qian of Yanci held a hundred thousand men in Douzi Dam.

sentences.zh: 充帥師破斬之，威振羣賊。

translations.literal: Shichong led his army, defeated and beheaded him, and his prestige shook the rebel hosts.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong crushed and beheaded him, terrifying the rebel hosts.

sentences.zh: 又擊盧明月，破之於南陽，斬首數萬，虜獲極多。

translations.literal: He also attacked Lu Mingyue, defeated him at Nanyang, cut off tens of thousands of heads, and captured booty in great quantity.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Lu Mingyue at Nanyang, taking tens of thousands of heads and vast booty.

sentences.zh: 後還江都，帝大悅，自執杯酒以賜之。

translations.literal: Later returning to Jiangdu, the emperor was greatly pleased and personally held a cup of wine to bestow on him.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to Jiangdu, the delighted emperor personally offered him a cup of wine.

sentences.zh: 時充又知帝好內，乃言江淮良家有美女，並願備後庭，無由自進。

translations.literal: At that time Shichong also knew the emperor loved women within the palace and said that good families of the Jiang-Huai region had beautiful daughters who all wished to enter the rear apartments but had no way to advance themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the emperor's appetite for women, Shichong said Jiang-Huai families had daughters eager for the inner palace who could not present themselves.

sentences.zh: 帝逾喜，因密令閱視諸女，姿質端麗合法相者，取正庫及應入京物以娉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor was even more pleased and therefore secretly ordered him to review the girls; those of fine appearance and proper physiognomy he took goods from the main treasury and items due for the capital to betroth them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor secretly ordered him to select beautiful women of proper physiognomy, paying betrothal gifts from the imperial treasury.

sentences.zh: 所用不可勝計，帳上云勑別用，不顯其實。

translations.literal: The expenditure was beyond counting; the accounts said "imperial order, separate use" and did not show the true amount.
translations.idiomatic: Expenditure was incalculable, recorded as separate imperial orders without showing true costs.

sentences.zh: 有合意者，則厚賞充；

translations.literal: If they pleased him he richly rewarded Shichong;
translations.idiomatic: Those who pleased the emperor richly rewarded Shichong;

sentences.zh: 或不中者，又以賚之。

translations.literal: if they did not suit him, he still gave them to Shichong as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: those who did not still became gifts to Shichong.

sentences.zh: 後令以船送東京，而道路賊起，使者苦役，於淮泗中沉船溺之者，前後十數。

translations.literal: Later he ordered them sent by boat to the eastern capital, but bandits rose on the roads; envoys suffered under corvée labor, and in the Huai-Si waters ships were sunk and people drowned—more than ten such cases in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Boats sent them eastward, but bandits harassed the route; envoys drowned ten or more shipments in the Huai-Si.

sentences.zh: 或有發露，充為秘之，又遽簡閱以供進。

translations.literal: When some were exposed, Shichong concealed it and hurriedly reviewed and supplied replacements for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: When losses were exposed Shichong concealed them and hurried fresh selections to court.

sentences.zh: 是後益見親昵。

translations.literal: After this he grew even more intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter intimacy deepened.

sentences.zh: 遇李密攻陷興洛倉，進逼東都，官軍數却，光祿大夫裴仁基以武牢降于密，帝惡之，大發兵，將討焉。

translations.literal: When Li Mi captured Xingluo granary and pressed the eastern capital, government troops were repeatedly driven back; Grand Master for Splendid Happiness Pei Renji surrendered Wulao to Mi; the emperor hated this and mobilized a great army to attack.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mi took Xingluo granary and threatened Luoyang, government troops fell back and Pei Renji surrendered Wulao; the emperor mobilized a great army.

sentences.zh: 發中詔遣充為將軍，於洛口以拒密，前後百餘戰，互有勝負。

translations.literal: An edict from within dispatched Shichong as general to resist Mi at Luokou; over a hundred battles followed, each side winning in turn.
translations.idiomatic: An inner edict made Shichong general at Luokou; over a hundred indecisive battles followed.

sentences.zh: 充乃引軍渡洛水，逼倉城。

translations.literal: Shichong then led his army across the Luo River and pressed the granary city.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong crossed the Luo and besieged the granary city.

sentences.zh: 李密與戰，充敗績，赴水溺死者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Li Mi fought him; Shichong was defeated and more than ten thousand drowned crossing the water.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi defeated him; more than ten thousand drowned crossing the river.

sentences.zh: 時天寒大雪，兵士既渡水，衣皆霑濕，在道凍死者又數萬人，比至河陽，纔以千數。

translations.literal: The weather was bitter cold with heavy snow; the soldiers having crossed the water, their clothes were soaked, and on the road tens of thousands more froze to death; by the time they reached Heyang only about a thousand remained.
translations.idiomatic: In bitter snow their soaked clothes froze tens of thousands more dead; only a thousand reached Heyang.

sentences.zh: 充自繫獄請罪，越王侗遣使赦之，召令還都。

translations.literal: Shichong bound himself and asked punishment; Prince Yue Tong sent envoys to pardon him and summoned him back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong asked punishment in bonds; Prince Yue Tong pardoned and recalled him.

sentences.zh: 收合亡散，復得萬餘人，屯於含嘉城中，不敢復出。

translations.literal: He gathered the scattered survivors and again obtained more than ten thousand, encamped in Hanjia city, and did not dare venture out again.
translations.idiomatic: He regathered ten thousand survivors in Hanjia city and dared not venture out.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及殺帝於江都，充與太府卿元文都、將軍皇甫無逸、右司郎盧楚奉侗為主。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Huaji killed the emperor at Jiangdu, Shichong together with Grand Treasury Minister Yuan Wendu, General Huangfu Wuyi, and Right Secretariat Attendant Lu Chu installed Tong as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji murdered the emperor at Jiangdu, Shichong with Yuan Wendu, Huangfu Wuyi, and Lu Chu enthroned Prince Yue Tong.

sentences.zh: 侗以充為吏部尚書，封鄭國公。

translations.literal: Tong appointed Shichong Minister of Personnel and enfeoffed him Duke of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Tong made Shichong minister of personnel and Duke of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 及侗取元文都、盧楚之謀，拜李密為太尉、尚書令，密遂稱臣，復以兵拒化及於黎陽，遣使告捷。

translations.literal: When Tong adopted the plans of Yuan Wendu and Lu Chu, appointing Li Mi Grand Marshal and Secretariat Director, Mi then styled himself minister and again with troops resisted Huaji at Liyang, sending envoys to report victory.
translations.idiomatic: Following Wendu and Lu Chu's plan, Tong appointed Li Mi grand marshal; Mi submitted, fought Huaji at Liyang, and reported victory.

sentences.zh: 眾皆悅，充獨謂其麾下諸將曰：「文都之輩，刀筆吏耳。

translations.literal: All were pleased; Shichong alone told his generals: "Wendu's crowd are mere clerks with pens.
translations.idiomatic: All rejoiced; Shichong alone told his generals: "Wendu's men are mere clerks.

sentences.zh: 吾觀其勢，必為李密所擒。

translations.literal: I see their situation—they will surely be captured by Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: They will surely fall to Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 且吾軍人每與密戰，殺其父兄子弟，前後已多，一旦為之下，吾屬無類矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover our soldiers have repeatedly fought Mi, killing his fathers, elder brothers, sons, and younger brothers—already many in number; once we submit to him, none of us will survive.
translations.idiomatic: Our men have killed Mi's kin in battle after battle; if we submit, none of us survives."

sentences.zh: 出此言以激怒其眾。

translations.literal: He spoke these words to enrage his followers.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke thus to enrage his troops.

sentences.zh: 文都知而大懼，與楚等謀，將因充入內，伏甲而殺之。

translations.literal: Wendu learned and was greatly afraid; with Chu and others he plotted to kill Shichong when he entered the palace by hiding armed men.
translations.idiomatic: Wendu, terrified, plotted with Chu to ambush Shichong when he entered the palace.

sentences.zh: 期有日矣，將軍段達遣其女婿張志以楚謀告之。

translations.literal: The day was fixed; General Duan Da had his son-in-law Zhang Zhi report Chu's plot.
translations.idiomatic: The day was set until Duan Da's son-in-law Zhang Zhi exposed Chu's plot.

sentences.zh: 充夜勒兵圍宮城，將軍費曜、田世闍等與戰於東太陽門外。

translations.literal: Shichong at night led troops to surround the palace; Generals Fei Yao and Tian Shikan fought him outside the East Taiyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong surrounded the palace at night; Fei Yao and Tian Shikan fought him at the East Taiyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 曜軍敗，充遂攻門而入，無逸以單騎遁走。

translations.literal: Yao's army was defeated; Shichong attacked through the gate; Wuyi fled alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Yao fell; Shichong broke in; Wuyi fled alone.

sentences.zh: 獲楚，殺之。

translations.literal: He captured Chu and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He seized and killed Chu.

sentences.zh: 時宮門尚閉，充令扣門言於侗曰：「元文都等欲執皇帝降于李密，段達知而以告臣。

translations.literal: The palace gates were still closed; Shichong ordered them knocked and said to Tong: "Yuan Wendu and the rest wished to seize the emperor and surrender to Li Mi; Duan Da learned and told me.
translations.idiomatic: Gates still closed, Shichong knocked and told Tong: "Wendu meant to hand you to Li Mi; Duan Da informed me.

sentences.zh: 臣非敢謀反，誅反者耳。」

translations.literal: Your servant does not dare rebel—I am killing rebels.
translations.idiomatic: I rebel not—I kill rebels."

sentences.zh: 文都聞變入，奉侗於乾陽殿，陳兵衞之。

translations.literal: Wendu heard of the upheaval and entered, escorting Tong to Qianyang Hall and arraying troops to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: Wendu rushed Tong to Qianyang Hall under guard.

sentences.zh: 令將帥乘城以拒難，兵敗，又獲文都殺之。

translations.literal: He ordered generals to man the walls to resist; the army was defeated and Wendu was again captured and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Generals manned the walls, failed, and Wendu was captured and killed.

sentences.zh: 侗命開門以納充，充悉遣人代宿衞者，乃入謁，頓首流涕而言曰：「文都等無狀，謀相屠害，事急為此，不敢背國。」

translations.literal: Tong ordered the gates opened to admit Shichong; Shichong sent men to replace all night guards, then entered to pay respects, prostrating himself with tears, saying: "Wendu and the rest were lawless, plotting mutual slaughter; affairs were urgent so I did this—I dare not betray the state."
translations.idiomatic: Tong opened the gates; Shichong replaced the night guards, prostrated himself weeping: "Wendu plotted massacre in extremity—I betray not the state."

sentences.zh: 侗與之盟。

translations.literal: Tong made a covenant with him.
translations.idiomatic: Tong swore a covenant with him.

sentences.zh: 充尋遣韋節等諷侗，令拜為尚書左僕射、總督內外諸軍事。

translations.literal: Before long Shichong sent Wei Jie and others to hint to Tong to appoint him Left Vice Minister and commander of all internal and external military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shichong had Wei Jie urge Tong to name him left vice minister and supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 又授其兄惲為內史令，入居禁中。

translations.literal: He also appointed his elder brother Yun Secretariat Director to dwell within the forbidden quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He installed his brother Yun as secretariat director within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 未幾，李密破化及還，其勁兵良馬多戰死，士卒皆倦。

translations.literal: Before long Li Mi defeated Huaji and returned; his crack troops and fine horses had mostly died in battle and the soldiers were all weary.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li Mi defeated Huaji; his best troops and horses were dead and his men exhausted.

sentences.zh: 充欲乘其敝而擊之，恐人不一，乃假託鬼神，言夢見周公，乃立祠於洛水之上，遣巫宣言周公欲令僕射急討李密，當有大功，不則兵皆疫死。

translations.literal: Shichong wished to strike their weakness but feared disunity; he therefore falsely invoked spirits, saying he dreamed of the Duke of Zhou, and erected a shrine on the Luo River, sending shamans to proclaim that the Duke of Zhou wished the Vice Minister to attack Li Mi quickly for great merit, otherwise all soldiers would die of plague.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing disunity, Shichong feigned a dream of the Duke of Zhou, built a shrine on the Luo, and had shamans declare attack Mi or all would die of plague.

sentences.zh: 充兵多楚人，俗信妖妄，故出此言以惑之。

translations.literal: Many of Shichong's troops were men of Chu; the custom believed in sorcery and delusion, so he spoke thus to confuse them.
translations.idiomatic: His Chu troops believed in omens, so he used this to sway them.

sentences.zh: 眾皆請戰。

translations.literal: All asked to fight.
translations.idiomatic: All clamored to fight.

sentences.zh: 充簡練精勇，得二萬餘人，馬千餘，遷營於洛水南。

translations.literal: Shichong selected and drilled elite troops, obtaining more than twenty thousand, over a thousand horses, and moved camp south of the Luo.
translations.idiomatic: He mustered twenty thousand elite troops and a thousand horses south of the Luo.

sentences.zh: 密軍偃師北山上。

translations.literal: Mi's army was on the northern mountain at Yanshi.
translations.idiomatic: Mi camped on the northern mountain at Yanshi.

sentences.zh: 時密新得志於化及，有輕充之心，不設壁壘。

translations.literal: At that time Mi had just triumphed over Huaji and held Shichong in contempt, establishing no ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh from defeating Huaji, Mi despised Shichong and built no defenses.

sentences.zh: 充夜遣二百餘騎潛入北山，伏溪谷中，令軍秣馬蓐食。

translations.literal: Shichong at night sent more than two hundred horsemen to infiltrate the northern mountain and hide in ravines, ordering the army to feed horses and take dry rations.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong sent two hundred horsemen to hide in ravines north of the mountain while troops took dry rations.

sentences.zh: 既而宵濟，人奔馬馳，遲明而薄密。

translations.literal: Then they crossed at night, men running and horses galloping; at dawn they pressed upon Mi.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed by night and struck at dawn.

sentences.zh: 密出兵應之，陣未成列而兩軍合戰，其伏兵蔽山而上，潛登北原，乘高下馳，壓密營。

translations.literal: Mi sent troops to meet them; the battle lines were not yet formed when the two armies joined; the ambush covered the mountain and ascended, secretly climbing the northern ridge, riding down from the heights and pressing Mi's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Mi met them before lines formed; ambushers climbed the ridge and swept down on Mi's camp.

sentences.zh: 營中亂，無能拒者，即入縱火。
