translations.literal: The camp fell into chaos and none could resist; they entered and set fires.
translations.idiomatic: Camp chaos followed; they entered and fired the camp.

sentences.zh: 密軍大驚而潰，降其將張童兒、陳智略，進下偃師。

translations.literal: Mi's army was greatly startled and routed; his generals Zhang Tong'er and Chen Zhilüe surrendered; Shichong advanced and took Yanshi.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's army routed; Zhang Tong'er and Chen Zhilüe surrendered; Shichong took Yanshi.

sentences.zh: 初，充兄偉及子玄應隨化及至東郡，密得而囚之於城中，至是，盡獲之。

translations.literal: Earlier Shichong's elder brother Wei and son Xuanying had followed Huaji to Dong commandery; Mi had captured and imprisoned them in the city—now all were recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Wei and son Xuanying, prisoners of Mi since following Huaji, were recovered.

sentences.zh: 又執密長史邴元真妻子、司馬鄭虔象之母及諸將子弟，皆撫慰之，各令潛呼其父兄。

translations.literal: He also seized the wives and children of Mi's chief clerk Xing Yuanzhen, his aide-de-camp Zheng Qianxiang's mother, and the sons and younger brothers of various generals, all comforting them and having each secretly call their fathers and elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He seized kin of Mi's officers, comforted them, and had them summon their men.

sentences.zh: 兵次洛口，邴元真、鄭虔象等舉倉城以應之。

translations.literal: When the army reached Luokou, Xing Yuanzhen, Zheng Qianxiang, and others raised the granary city in response.
translations.idiomatic: At Luokou, Yuanzhen and Qianxiang opened the granary city to him.

sentences.zh: 密以數十騎遁逸，充悉收其眾。

translations.literal: Mi fled with several dozen horsemen; Shichong gathered all his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Mi fled with dozens of horsemen; Shichong absorbed his entire force.

sentences.zh: 而東盡于海，南至于江，悉來歸附。

translations.literal: Eastward to the sea and southward to the Yangtze, all came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: From the sea to the Yangtze, all submitted.

sentences.zh: 充又令韋節諷侗，拜為太尉，署置官屬，以尚書省為其府。

translations.literal: Shichong again had Wei Jie hint to Tong to appoint him Grand Marshal, establish officials, and take the Secretariat as his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jie urged Tong to make him grand marshal with the secretariat as his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 尋自稱鄭王。

translations.literal: Soon he styled himself King of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he styled himself King of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 遣其將高略帥師攻壽安，不利而旋。

translations.literal: He sent his general Gao Lüe to attack Shou'an with troops; it went badly and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: General Gao Lüe attacked Shou'an unsuccessfully.

sentences.zh: 又帥師攻圍穀州，三日而退。

translations.literal: He again led troops to besiege Gu prefecture and withdrew after three days.
translations.idiomatic: He besieged Gu prefecture three days and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明年，自稱相國，受九錫備物，是後不朝侗矣。

translations.literal: The next year he styled himself Chancellor, received the Nine Bestowals and full regalia, and thereafter no longer attended audience with Tong.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became chancellor with the Nine Bestowals and ceased attending Tong.

sentences.zh: 有道士桓法嗣者，自言解圖讖，充昵之。

translations.literal: There was a Daoist Huan Fasi who claimed to interpret prophecies; Shichong was intimate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Daoist Huan Fasi, claiming prophecy skill, won Shichong's favor.

sentences.zh: 法嗣乃以孔子閉房記，畫作丈夫持一干以驅羊。

translations.literal: Fasi took Confucius's Closed-Room Record and painted a man holding a single pole driving sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Fasi painted from Confucius's Closed-Room Record a man with one pole driving sheep.

sentences.zh: 法嗣云：「楊，隋姓也。

translations.literal: Fasi said: "Yang is the surname of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Fasi said: "Yang is Sui's surname.

sentences.zh: 干一者，王字也。

translations.literal: The single pole is the character wang [king].
translations.idiomatic: The single pole forms the character for 'king.'

sentences.zh: 居羊後，明相國代隋為帝也。」

translations.literal: Placed after sheep, it shows the Chancellor will replace Sui as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: After 'sheep' it shows the chancellor replacing Sui as emperor."

sentences.zh: 又取莊子人間世、德充符二篇上之，法嗣釋曰：「上篇言世，下篇言充，此即相國名矣。

translations.literal: He also presented the Zhuangzi chapters "Human Affairs in the World" and "Signs of Full Virtue"; Fasi explained: "The upper chapter speaks of shi [affairs/world], the lower of chong [full]; this is the Chancellor's name.
translations.idiomatic: He cited Zhuangzi's 'Human Affairs' and 'Full Virtue'; Fasi read shi and chong as Shichong's name.

sentences.zh: 明當德被人間，而應符命為天子也。」

translations.literal: It shows he will embody virtue among the people and respond to the mandate as Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: It prophesied virtue among the people and mandate as Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 充大悅曰：「此天命也。」

translations.literal: Shichong was greatly pleased and said: "This is Heaven's command."
translations.idiomatic: Shichong rejoiced: "This is Heaven's command."

sentences.zh: 再拜受之。

translations.literal: He bowed twice and received it.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed twice and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 即以法嗣為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He at once appointed Fasi Remonstrating Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: He made Fasi remonstrating counselor.

sentences.zh: 充又羅取雜鳥，書帛繫其頸，自言符命而散放之。

translations.literal: Shichong also gathered assorted birds, tied silk with writing to their necks claiming mandate, and released them.
translations.idiomatic: He tied prophecy silk to birds' necks and released them.

sentences.zh: 或有彈射得鳥而來獻者，亦拜官爵。

translations.literal: If someone shot down a bird and brought it, he also bestowed rank and title.
translations.idiomatic: Those who shot down birds and presented them received rank.

sentences.zh: 既而廢侗於別宮，僭即皇帝位，建元曰開明，國號鄭。

translations.literal: Before long he deposed Tong in a separate palace, usurped the imperial throne, established the era name Kaiming, and named the state Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: He deposed Tong, seized the throne, adopted era Kaiming, and named his state Zheng.

sentences.zh: 大唐遣秦王率眾圍之，充頻出兵，戰輒不利，都外諸城相繼降款。

translations.literal: The Great Tang sent the Prince of Qin at the head of masses to besiege him; Shichong repeatedly sent out troops, was defeated in every battle, and the cities outside the capital surrendered one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Tang's Prince of Qin besieged him; every sortie failed and outer cities surrendered.

sentences.zh: 充窘迫，遣使請救於竇建德，建德率精兵援之。

translations.literal: Shichong in distress sent to Dou Jiande for rescue; Jiande led crack troops to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: Desperate, Shichong summoned Dou Jiande, who marched elite troops to his aid.

sentences.zh: 師至武牢，為秦王所破，擒建德以詣城下。

translations.literal: When the army reached Wulao it was broken by the Prince of Qin; Jiande was captured and brought below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: At Wulao the Prince of Qin shattered Jiande's army and displayed him beneath the walls.

sentences.zh: 充將潰圍而出，諸將莫有應之者，自知潛竄無所，於是出降。

translations.literal: Shichong wished to break out of the encirclement but none of his generals responded; knowing stealthy escape was impossible, he therefore came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong meant to break out but no general followed; seeing escape impossible, he surrendered.

sentences.zh: 至長安，為讎人獨孤修德所殺。

translations.literal: Reaching Chang'an, he was killed by his enemy Dugu Xiude.
translations.idiomatic: At Chang'an his enemy Dugu Xiude killed him.

sentences.zh: 段達，武威姑臧人也。

translations.literal: Duan Da—Duan Da was a man of Guzang in Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Da was from Guzang in Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 父嚴，周朔州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yan was Zhou prefect of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan was Zhou prefect of Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 達在周，年始三歲，襲爵襄垣縣公。

translations.literal: Da in Zhou, at the age of three, inherited the title Duke of Xiangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou, Da at age three inherited the dukedom of Xiangyuan.

sentences.zh: 及長，身長八尺，美鬚髯，便弓馬。

translations.literal: When grown he was eight feet tall, with a fine beard, skilled at bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he stood eight feet with a fine beard, expert at bow and horse.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，以大都督領親信兵，常置左右。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was Chancellor, he as Grand Commander led trusted troops and was constantly placed at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was chancellor, Da as grand commander led trusted troops at his side.

sentences.zh: 及踐阼，為左直齋，累遷車騎將軍，兼晉王參軍。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, he became Left Direct Guard; he was repeatedly promoted to Cavalry General and concurrently aide to the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: On accession he became left direct guard, rose to cavalry general and aide to the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 高智惠、李積等之作亂也，達率眾一萬，擊定方、滁二州，賜縑千段，遷進儀同。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhihui, Li Ji, and others rebelled, Da led ten thousand men and pacified Fang and Chu prefectures, was given a thousand bolts of silk, and was promoted to Honored Companion.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified Fang and Chu in Gao Zhihui's rebellion, received a thousand bolts of silk, and rose to honored companion.

sentences.zh: 又破汪文進等於宣州，加開府，賜奴婢五十口，緜絹四千段。

translations.literal: He again defeated Wang Wenjin and others at Xuanzhou, was given the title of Opening the Government, fifty household slaves, and four thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Wang Wenjin at Xuanzhou, received opening-the-government rank, fifty slaves, and four thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，太子左衞副率。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renshou he was Deputy Leader of the Crown Prince's Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At Renshou's start he was deputy leader of the crown prince's left guard.

sentences.zh: 大業初，以蕃邸之舊，拜左翊衞將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye, because of old ties from the prince's household, he was appointed General of the Left Yiwu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Daye, old ties from the prince's household won him general of the Left Yiwu Guard.

sentences.zh: 征吐谷渾，進位金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: On the Tuyuhun campaign he was promoted to Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: On the Tuyuhun campaign he rose to grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 帝征遼東，百姓苦役，平原祁孝德、清河張金稱等並聚眾為羣盜，攻陷城邑，郡縣不能禦。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned in Liaodong the people suffered under corvée; Qi Xiaode of Pingyuan, Zhang Jinching of Qinghe, and others all gathered hosts as bandits, seized cities, and prefectures and counties could not defend.
translations.idiomatic: On the Liaodong campaign corvée broke the people; Qi Xiaode, Zhang Jinching, and others seized cities prefectures could not hold.

sentences.zh: 帝令達擊之，數為金稱等所挫，亡失甚多。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Da to attack them; he was several times thwarted by Jinching and others and lost many men.
translations.idiomatic: Da attacked them but Jinching repeatedly defeated him with heavy losses.

sentences.zh: 諸賊輕之，號為段姥。

translations.literal: The bandits despised him and called him "Old Lady Duan."
translations.idiomatic: Bandits mocked him as "Old Lady Duan."

sentences.zh: 後用鄃令楊善會之計，更與賊戰，方致剋捷。

translations.literal: Later using the plan of Yuxian magistrate Yang Shanhui, he fought the bandits again and finally achieved victory.
translations.idiomatic: Later, using magistrate Yang Shanhui's plan, he finally won.

sentences.zh: 還京師，以公事坐免。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he was dismissed from office for a public-affairs offense.
translations.idiomatic: Back at the capital he was dismissed for an official offense.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝征遼東，以達留守涿郡。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor campaigned in Liaodong and left Da to garrison Zhuo commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, on the Liaodong campaign, the emperor left Da to hold Zhuo commandery.

sentences.zh: 俄復拜左翊衞將軍。

translations.literal: Before long he was again appointed General of the Left Yiwu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored as general of the Left Yiwu Guard.

sentences.zh: 高陽魏刀兒聚眾十餘萬，自號歷山飛，寇掠燕、趙。

translations.literal: Wei Dao'er of Gaoyang gathered more than a hundred thousand followers, styled himself Lishan Flying, and raided Yan and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Dao'er of Gaoyang raised a hundred thousand men, styled himself Lishan Flying, and ravaged Yan and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 達率涿郡通守郭絢擊敗之。

translations.literal: Da led Zhuo commandery transit intendant Guo Xuan and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Da with Zhuo transit intendant Guo Xuan defeated him.

sentences.zh: 于時盜賊既多，官軍惡戰，達不能因機決勝，唯持重自守，頓兵饋糧，多無剋獲，時皆謂之為怯愞。

translations.literal: At that time bandits were numerous and government troops hated battle; Da could not seize opportunity for victory but only held his ground cautiously, halting troops and wasting grain, often gaining nothing—everyone called him timid and weak.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits multiplied and troops loathed fighting; Da could not seize openings but camped cautiously, wasting grain with few victories, and men called him timid.

sentences.zh: 十二年，帝幸江都宮，詔達與太府卿元文都留守東都。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the emperor visited the Jiangdu palace and ordered Da and Grand Treasury Minister Yuan Wendu to remain and guard the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve the emperor went to Jiangdu and left Da with Grand Treasury Minister Yuan Wendu to guard Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 李密據洛口，縱兵侵掠城下，達與監門郎將龐玉、武牙郎將霍舉率內兵出禦之。

translations.literal: Li Mi held Luokou and sent troops to raid below the walls; Da with Gate Guard Gentleman Pang Yu and Martial Tooth Gentleman Huo Ju led inner troops out to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi held Luokou and raided the walls; Da with Pang Yu and Huo Ju led palace troops out to resist.

sentences.zh: 頗有功，遷左驍衞大將軍。

translations.literal: He achieved considerable merit and was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Left Xiao Guard.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was made general-in-chief of the Left Xiao Guard.

sentences.zh: 王充之敗也，密復進據北芒，來至上春門，達與判左丞郭文懿、尚書韋津出兵拒之。

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong was defeated, Mi again advanced to hold Beimang and came to the Shangchun Gate; Da with Acting Left Vice Director Guo Wanyi and Minister Wei Jin led troops out to resist.
translations.idiomatic: After Shichong's defeat Mi seized Beimang and reached Shangchun Gate; Da with Guo Wanyi and Minister Wei Jin marched out to resist.

sentences.zh: 達見賊盛，不陣而走，為密所乘，軍大潰，津沒於陣。

translations.literal: Da saw the rebels strong, fled without forming battle lines, was exploited by Mi, the army routed in great collapse, and Jin perished in the battle.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the rebels strong, Da fled without forming lines; Mi exploited it, the army routed, and Jin died in battle.

sentences.zh: 由是賊勢日盛。

translations.literal: Because of this the rebel strength grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel strength grew daily thereafter.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩於江都，達與元文都等推越王侗為主，署開府儀同三司，兼納言，封陳國公。

translations.literal: When the emperor died at Jiangdu, Da with Yuan Wendu and others installed Prince Yue Tong as ruler, appointed him Opening the Government with Honored Companion of the Third Rank, concurrently Chief Speaker, and enfeoffed him Duke of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died at Jiangdu, Da with Wendu enthroned Prince Yue Tong, made him opening-the-government honored companion, chief speaker, and Duke of Chen.

sentences.zh: 元文都等謀誅王充也，達陰告充，為之內應。

translations.literal: When Yuan Wendu and others plotted to kill Wang Shichong, Da secretly informed Shichong and acted as his inside collaborator.
translations.idiomatic: When Wendu plotted to kill Shichong, Da secretly informed him and served as inside collaborator.

sentences.zh: 及事發，越王侗執文都於充，充甚德於達，特見崇重。

translations.literal: When the affair broke out, Prince Yue Tong handed Wendu over to Shichong; Shichong was deeply grateful to Da and showed him special honor and weight.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot erupted Tong handed Wendu to Shichong, who richly rewarded Da with special honor.

sentences.zh: 既破李密，達等勸越王加充九錫備物，尋諷令禪讓。

translations.literal: After defeating Li Mi, Da and others urged Prince Yue to grant Shichong the Nine Bestowals and full regalia, and soon hinted that he should abdicate.
translations.idiomatic: After Mi's defeat Da urged Tong to grant Shichong the Nine Bestowals and soon hinted abdication.

sentences.zh: 充僭尊號，以達為司徒。

translations.literal: When Shichong usurped the exalted title, he made Da Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When Shichong seized the throne he made Da minister of education.

sentences.zh: 及東都平，坐誅，妻子籍沒。

translations.literal: When the eastern capital was pacified, he was executed for his crime; wife and children were registered and confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell he was executed and his family confiscated.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：化及庸愞下才，負恩累葉，王充斗筲小器，遭逢時幸，俱蒙奬擢，禮越舊臣。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Huaji was mediocre and dull, a talent of the lower rank, ungrateful through successive generations; Wang Shichong was a petty vessel of a peck and dipper, who met with timely fortune; both received reward and promotion, their ritual precedence surpassing old ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Huaji was a mediocre ingrate of low talent; Shichong a petty man favored by fortune; both were promoted above veteran ministers.

sentences.zh: 既屬崩剝之期，不能致身竭命，乃因利乘便，先圖干紀，率羣不逞，職為亂階，拔本塞源，裂冠毀冕。

translations.literal: When the age of collapse and dismemberment arrived, they could not devote their persons and exhaust their lives; instead they seized advantage from profit and convenience, first plotting violation of the norm, leading the unruly masses, serving as steps to chaos, uprooting the root and blocking the source, tearing the cap and destroying the regalia.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty crumbled they would not die for it but seized advantage, led rebels, uprooted order, and tore the crown from the state.

sentences.zh: 或躬為戎首，或親行鴆毒，釁深指鹿，事切食蹯，天地所不容，人神所同憤。

translations.literal: Some personally became leaders of war, some personally administered poison; their guilt was deep as calling a deer a horse, their deeds urgent as eating one's foot—heaven and earth could not contain them, men and spirits alike raged against them.
translations.idiomatic: Some led armies themselves, some poisoned their lord; their crimes were as brazen as calling a deer a horse—heaven, earth, and all mankind raged against them.

sentences.zh: 故梟獍凶魁，相尋葅戮，蛇豕醜類，繼踵誅夷，快忠義於當年，垂炯戒於來葉。

translations.literal: Therefore the owl-and-porridge wicked chiefs were minced and executed in succession, the snake-and-pig vile sort exterminated one after another, satisfying loyalty and righteousness in their own day and leaving a bright warning for generations to come.
translations.idiomatic: Thus these owl-hearted villains were minced in turn, these serpent swine exterminated one after another, satisfying justice then and warning generations yet to come.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，為人臣者可不殷鑒哉！

translations.literal: Alas—how can those who serve as ministers fail to take this as a stern mirror!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—how can any minister fail to heed this stern warning!

sentences.zh: 可不殷鑒哉！

translations.literal: How can one fail to take this as a stern mirror!
translations.idiomatic: How can one fail to heed this warning!
